expectations.text: A documentation plan, index, or master file is produced that explicitly maps stakeholders or personas to specific documents (e.g., a section like 'For new engineers: X, Y' / 'For ops: Z' OR a table with columns like Audience/Persona × Document). A flat list of files without stakeholder mapping does NOT satisfy this.
expectations.evidence: HANDOFF.md §2 'Documentation Index' contains a table with columns 'File | Audience | Read First?' that explicitly maps each document to its target stakeholder: README.md → Everyone, ONBOARDING.md → All engineers, ARCHITECTURE.md → Engineers, DEVELOPMENT.md → Engineers, API.md → Backend engineers, DATABASE.md → Engineers + ops, DEPLOYMENT.md → Engineers + ops, RUNBOOK.md → Ops primarily, TROUBLESHOOTING.md → Everyone. The final output.txt also summarizes this as a 'Primary Audience' column.

expectations.text: The plan uses explicit prioritization markers — at minimum TWO distinct priority tiers must be visible using one of these schemes: P0/P1/P2, must-have/nice-to-have, critical/important/optional, MVP/extended, tier-1/tier-2, or numbered phases (Phase 1/Phase 2). An undifferentiated bullet list of docs without any priority annotation does NOT satisfy this.
expectations.evidence: No P0/P1/P2, must-have/nice-to-have, critical/important/optional, MVP/extended, tier-1/tier-2, or Phase 1/Phase 2 markers appear anywhere in HANDOFF.md (confirmed by regex scan: 0 matches). The 'Read First?' column uses timing-based guidance (Yes, Week 1, Week 1–2, Before going on-call, On demand) and §3 'Recommended Handoff Schedule' uses 'Week 1 — Orientation', 'Week 2 — Supervised Operation', 'Week 3 — Independent' — these are temporal sequencing indicators, not priority tiers per any of the specified schemes.

expectations.text: At least FOUR distinct documentation files are produced beyond the plan itself (i.e., 5+ files total counting the plan). Acceptable examples: README, ARCHITECTURE, RUNBOOK, ONBOARDING, OPERATIONS, API, DEPLOYMENT, TROUBLESHOOTING, CONTRIBUTING. A plan-only output or a plan + 1-2 docs does NOT satisfy this.
expectations.evidence: 10 files were written total: HANDOFF.md (plan/master), README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, ONBOARDING.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, DATABASE.md, API.md, RUNBOOK.md, TROUBLESHOOTING.md. That is 9 files beyond the plan, well exceeding the threshold of 4 additional files.

claims.evidence: Full table content extracted from HANDOFF.md Write call in transcript: File | Audience | Read First? table with 9 rows mapping each doc to a specific audience

suggestions.assertion: The plan uses explicit prioritization markers — at minimum TWO distinct priority tiers must be visible
suggestions.reason: The 'Read First?' column in the Documentation Index table (Yes / Week 1 / Week 1–2 / On demand) comes close to functioning as priority tiers. The eval could acknowledge temporal sequencing as a borderline case, or alternatively require that the expectation text explicitly exclude timing-based schemes to make the boundary unambiguous.

No assertion checks whether the individual documentation files (README, RUNBOOK, etc.) contain substantive content beyond placeholder text. A run that writes 10 nearly-empty stubs would pass expectation 3 but produce no real value.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1 and 3 are well-constructed and discriminating. Assertion 2 (priority tiers) has an edge case around temporal sequencing that could benefit from clarification in the eval text.
